Switched memory B.description: Memory B cells that have undergone class switch recombination, typically expressing CD27 and lacking surface IgD.

Unswitched memory B.description: Memory B cells that have not undergone class switch recombination, co-expressing surface IgM and IgD along with CD27.

Naive B.description: Mature B cells that have not encountered antigen, expressing surface IgD and IgM, lacking CD27.

Plasma cells.description: Antibody-secreting effector B cells characterized by high CD38 and surface or intracellular immunoglobulin.

Classical Monocyte.description: Classical CD14++CD16- monocytes are the most abundant monocyte subset, responsible for phagocytosis, cytokine production, and inflammation.

Non-classical Monocyte.description: Non-classical CD14+CD16++ monocytes patrol the endothelium, produce anti-inflammatory cytokines, and respond to viral and nucleic acid stimuli.

Intermediate Monocyte.description: Intermediate CD14++CD16+ monocytes exhibit both classical and non-classical features, with high antigen-presenting and inflammatory cytokine production.

CD1c+ Dendritic Cell.description: CD1c+ myeloid dendritic cells (cDC2) are professional antigen-presenting cells that activate T cells and produce cytokines in response to pathogens.

CD141+ Dendritic Cell.description: CD141+ myeloid dendritic cells (cDC1) specialize in cross-presentation and are crucial for antiviral and antitumor immunity.
